findings.message: `_authorize_backfill_in_path` re-implements the `DagDetails`/`get_team_name`/`is_authorized_dag` sequence that `requires_access_dag` already performs, so the two authorization paths can silently drift apart the next time `requires_access_dag` gains a check. Consider delegating to `requires_access_dag` and translating its 403 into the 404 you want, rather than keeping a parallel copy.

When the path carries a `backfill_id` that this adapter rejects, control still falls through to the body/query branch, so a route that names a backfill in its path ends up authorized against a caller-supplied `dag_id`. That is the same shape of issue this PR closes, and it is only harmless as long as the handler's parser stays exactly as strict. Better to fail closed here: if `backfill_id_raw` is present but unparseable, raise rather than reaching the body path.

This fixture reaches into `auth_manager._get_token_signer()` and patches `RevokedToken.is_revoked` to mint a viewer token by hand. If there is an existing helper for building a role-scoped test client, prefer it — a private-API test fixture will break the next time the token plumbing is refactored.
